title: Count Static and Streaming Islands
prompt:
### Part 1

Implement `count_islands(grid) -> int` for a rectangular list of integer rows containing only `0` (water) and `1` (land). An island connects land through the four orthogonal directions; diagonals do not connect. Empty grids return `0`. Do not mutate `grid`. Target `O(R*C)` time; use iterative traversal to avoid recursion-depth limits.

### Part 2

Implement `streaming_islands(rows, cols, positions) -> list[int]`. Start with an all-water grid and add land at each `[row, column]` in `positions`. Return the island count after every operation. Repeated additions do nothing. Dimensions are nonnegative integers; every supplied position is valid and zero-indexed. If a dimension is zero, positions is empty. Inputs are not mutated.

Use sparse union-find: allocate storage only for added cells, not `rows*cols`. Target `O(k * alpha(k))` amortized time and `O(k)` space for `k` operations. Decrement the count only on merging two distinct roots; touching multiple neighbors in one existing island must not over-decrement.

Practice reconstruction: static representation, coordinate order, valid-input scope and mutation policy are explicit conventions. Both parts share the same four-neighbor island definition.

example.reasoning: Diagonal cells begin separately; the bridge joins them; a duplicate is a no-op.
